September 1949
Treasury Financing Operations
Refundings in September, October, and December

The announcement was made by the Secretary of the Treasury on August 22 that a new one-year 1-1/8 percent certificate of indebtedness would be offered on August 31 to the holders of the 2 percent Treasury bonds of September 15, 1949-51. The bonds, outstanding in the amount of $1,292 million, had been called on May 13 for redemption September 15. Subsequently, it was announced that the new certificate issue would be dated September 15, 1949.

The Secretary's announcement on August 22 stated also that a new certificate of indebtedness would be offered to refund the certificates maturing on October 1, 1949; and that a new Treasury note would be offered in connection with the refunding of the Treasury bonds called for redemption on December 15, 1949.
The certificates maturing October 1 were issued October 1, 1948, and bear interest at 1-1/4 percent. They are outstanding in the amount of $6,535 million.
Call of Three Issues of Treasury Bonds for December 15

With respect to the refunding of the Treasury bonds on December 15, the Secretary announced on August 12 that all outstanding Treasury bonds of three issues are called for redemption on December 15, 1949. The amounts outstanding total $4,375 million.

Note: Details of Treasury market financing operations are shown in the tables on "Offerings" and "Disposition", respectively, of marketable issues of bonds, notes, and certificates of indebtedness, and in the table "Offerings of Treasury Bills", in this issue of the "Treasury Bulletin".

Treasury Bills Refunded and Increased

Treasury bills matured in August in the amount of $3.4 billion, and new offerings totaled $4.0 billion. The first and third maturing issues amounted to $800 million each, and both the second and fourth maturing issues amounted to $900 million. Each of the four new offerings was for $1.0 billion. The successive average rates of discount on the weekly issues, beginning with that dated August 4, were 1.032 percent, 1.007 percent, 1.017 percent, and 1.031 percent.
Treasury Savings Notes, Series D

An amendment to the terms relating to the purchase of Treasury savings notes, Series D was announced on August 10. Effective August 11, 1949, Treasury savings notes, Series D, are sold at par and accrued interest from the first day of the month in which purchased to the day, inclusive, on which full payment is made in cash or other immediately available funds.

The amount of accrued interest payable by the purchaser will be computed at the rate at which interest accrues on the notes ($0.80 per month per $1,000 par amount) for the actual number of days in the month in which the purchase is made.

CAPITAL MOVEMENTS

Information relating to capital movements between the United States and foreign countries is presented in four sections. Section I presents first a historical summary of the principal types of data on capital movements, beginning with 1935 when the information was first compiled. Each type of data is then broken down into its chief components in the same chronological detail.

Section II supplies a geographic breakdown by principal countries for recent months. The total net capital movement is given first and then the principal categories are shown separately. In addition, at this point, the total outstanding claims on and liabilities to foreign countries are each presented.
Section III presents details with respect to capital movements and short-term claims and liabilities. These are shown for the latest month for which final data are
available and the latest month for which preliminary data are available.
Section IV contains data for recent months on outstanding contracts of banks for forward purchases and sales of foreign exchange.

The data in these four sections are based on reports filed each month by banks, bankers, and brokers throughout the United States. The reports are collected, checked, and tabulated by the twelve Federal Reserve Banks. The totals are then forwarded to the Treasury Department for consolidation and publication.

Publication of detailed figures on capital movements was discontinued between the March 1942 and the November 1945 issues of the "Treasury Bulletin", but data omitted during that period were supplied in the November 1945 issue and supplement.
